fields.description:
Every citation below describes the tree at commit `6c3f13a`, the base this work branches from.

At `6c3f13a`, `to_host_url` and `to_host_hostport` in `scripts/config.py` rewrote a Compose service name to `localhost` but carried the original port through unchanged. That is only correct while every service publishes on the host under the same number it listens on inside the network.

At `6c3f13a`, `compose.yaml` hardcoded each published port, for example `ports: ["5432:5432"]` for postgres and `ports: ["3000:3000"]` for langfuse-web. An operator whose host already uses those numbers must remap them in an overlay. Once remapped, the rewrite produced an address that does not answer. On the pilot machine postgres publishes 15432, so `postgresql://platform@postgres:5432/agent_platform` rewrote to `localhost:5432` and every host-run database tool failed.

The hardcoded ports were the root cause. The rewrite had no way to learn the published number because nothing recorded it outside the compose file.

At `6c3f13a`, `database/migrations/env.py` and `scripts/db_reset.py` each read `ALEMBIC_DATABASE_URL` directly with a `localhost:5432` default, bypassing the rewrite entirely, so a remapped port broke migrations run from the host as well.

Parameterising each published port with an environment variable that defaults to the value in use gives the compose file and the rewrite a single source of truth, and removes the need for an overlay to override ports at all.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] A Compose service URL rewrites to the published host port when that port is remapped, proven by `pytest tests/unit/test_config_host_rewrite.py -k host_url_uses_the_published_port_when_remapped`
- [x] A Compose service URL keeps its port when no remap is configured, proven by `pytest tests/unit/test_config_host_rewrite.py -k host_url_keeps_the_default_port_when_unmapped`
- [x] A rewritten URL preserves user credentials, proven by `pytest tests/unit/test_config_host_rewrite.py -k host_url_preserves_credentials_across_the_port_remap`
- [x] A Compose host:port value rewrites to the published host port when remapped, proven by `pytest tests/unit/test_config_host_rewrite.py -k host_hostport_uses_the_published_port_when_remapped`
- [x] A non-Compose hostname is returned unchanged, proven by `pytest tests/unit/test_config_host_rewrite.py -k host_url_leaves_a_foreign_hostname_alone`
- [x] The rewrite stays inert inside the platform image, proven by `pytest tests/unit/test_config_host_rewrite.py -k host_url_is_inert_inside_the_platform_image`
- [x] Every Compose service that the rewrite recognises publishes its port through a variable, proven by `pytest tests/unit/test_config_host_rewrite.py -k every_rewritable_service_publishes_through_a_variable`
- [x] The migration URL follows the published Postgres port, proven by `pytest tests/unit/test_config_host_rewrite.py -k alembic_database_url_follows_the_published_postgres_port`
- [x] A configured migration URL naming the Compose service is rewritten for the host, proven by `pytest tests/unit/test_config_host_rewrite.py -k alembic_database_url_rewrites_a_configured_service_address`
- [x] The collector's three published ports map independently of one another, proven by `pytest tests/unit/test_config_host_rewrite.py -k otel_collector_maps_each_of_its_three_ports_separately`
- [x] A bare Compose service name with no port rewrites to a bare localhost, proven by `pytest tests/unit/test_config_host_rewrite.py -k host_hostport_returns_a_bare_service_name_without_a_port`
- [x] A Compose service URL with no port keeps its portless form, proven by `pytest tests/unit/test_config_host_rewrite.py -k host_url_without_a_port_gains_none`

## Testing
Run each acceptance criterion selector on its own. Run `PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" .venv/bin/inv ci` before closing the ticket.
